Two height contradictions combine exact three-mode radical coverage, contact-height19, scalar/anchor cutoffs and the inherited Lucas exponential lower bound. They first force F(s,t,z)=0, then 2 beta=n; lowest terms force X integral.

General roots use doubled integer indices via the existing generator/torsion classification and explicit 2R=P*. Duplication height bounds give n²/4; charts preserve nonzero domains. Scalar logarithm identity uses actual doubled points and unramified inert as well as split primes.
The retained two-place anchor, with its explicit 3-adic valuation, supplies the enlarged cutoffs for H*=5H. Both beta comparisons must consume 2 beta; the scalar polynomial remains beta=X²+2.

Target-two soundness uses actual doubled differences and denominator order to force h a p-adic unit. Completeness uses full finite group orders with gcd4 and doubling images, then independent per-contact CRT; no cyclicity, reduction surjectivity or cross-prime compatibility is assumed. Explicit fixed-target coefficients require full incidence checks.

Tangent fusion proves y nonzero from the curve and restores the inverse, including curve preservation under doubling. Shared square evaluation is an exact no-division substitution preserving original order-one F test, not a relabeling as a square test.

First norm fusion first changes the arithmetic denominator using a sharper odd-parity valuation deduction, then applies an exact rational projection guarded by conic r nonzero. Completeness retains depth2 and unit root; all other leaves and shared fields unchanged.

Selected-source equivalence composes ordered constructions: scalar/anchor, Lucas roots, fixed coefficients, prime exclusions, common J and private CRT points, fields then conics/poles. Reverse implication decodes arbitrary odd contacts without ordinariness and uses two height contradictions. Compiler sums of squares do not replace arithmetic premises.

Finite G9/G2 evaluation uses exact quadratic identities and nonzero rational a6, distinct from approximation estimates. The4935-coordinate source digest, complete flattening and module audit certify finite identities only; rational projection is the preceding conditional arithmetic theorem.

Allowed reductions have explicit forward/reverse rational maps: nonzero constant definitions, invertible row/shear changes, elimination modulo retained rows and exact power circuits. Complete current incidence, fresh coordinates, degree2 and unchanged input are essential.

Parity-block replacement checks b=0 and u=-b exceptional branches explicitly. Sign change of private U is allowed; maps establish existential projection equality, not inverse private tuples. Rule is limited to height-parity blocks, not ordinary pole.

Quartic realization requires the exact551-event certificate, current supports, variable bijection and full collected expansion. Sum-of-squares equivalence and degree/count claims concern one selected polynomial; finite verification does not prove inherited rank, height, primes, formal group or pole inputs.
